prerequisites: Knowledge of the basic concepts and techniques of mathematical analysis: study and plotting of functions, derivation and integration.
Basic elements of physics: Newton equation of translational and rotational dynamics, Kirchhoff laws.

learning_outcomes.text: Provide a unitary method of classification and study of cause-effect relationships in dynamic systems through the use of mathematical models.
Deepen the methods for the analysis of linear and time-invariant dynamical systems in the time domain and in the frequency domain.
Represent nonlinear systems through linearization by analyzing case studies: an electrical circuit with a constant-power load, a predator-prey model, and an SIR model.
Acquire skills on the analysis of dynamic systems through computer simulation.
Recognize the dynamic nature of a system based on its input-output behavior.
Apply time-domain and frequency-domain models to electrical and mechanical systems.
Evaluate/interpret the importance of the dynamic analysis of a physical phenomenon.
Communicate the behavioral characteristics of a dynamic system.
Develop the ability to explore the dynamic behavior of systems in greater depth, including through numerical analysis.

syllabus_topics: The concepts of system and model
The Laplace transform: exponential, step, ramp, impulse
Theorems on the Laplace transform: real derivation, final value, initial value, real integration
Transfer function and impulse response function
Models of electrical, mechanical, electromechanical, thermal and hydraulic systems
Time response to impulse, step, ramp, sinusoid
First order, second order and higher order systems
Nonlinear systems and linearization: electric circuit with constant-power load, predator-prey model, SIR model
Simulation of dynamical systems with Matlab and Simulink
teaching_methods: Lectures (using the blackboard; slides used occasionally)
Practical exercises (using the blackboard and computers or AI)
assessment_rules: The final examination consists of a written test and an oral interview. The assessment criteria include relevance of answers, quality of content, appropriate use of technical terminology, expressive ability, ability to connect topics, and ability to provide examples. Students with specific learning disorders, disabilities, or other educational needs can agree upon assessment arrangements.
